paragraphs: Friend, here's what I take from all that measuring. God cares about the details of a place where He is to be approached. Walls, rooms and doors are all measured, and the man even ends by measuring the whole area on all four sides: five hundred cubits each (Ezekiel 42:15-20). I can barely keep track of which drawer my tape measure is in, and God is out here with a rod and a plan!

Then the passage tells us why the wall is there: "to separate the holy from the common." (Ezekiel 42:20) The same idea shows up in the priests' clothes. They must leave their ministering garments behind, "for these are holy." (Ezekiel 42:14) So this is a place where drawing near to the LORD is taken seriously, and the holy things are treated as holy.

So what does that mean for you, baker? It means you can come to God with reverence, and you can come knowing He has made a way to meet with people. The man even calls the wooden altar "the table that is before the LORD." (Ezekiel 41:22) That's my kind of furniture, friend, a table set in His presence. And this tour isn't over, so keep your apron on!
